teenKit.tldr: An unregulated supplement tricked the body into faking a normal blood sugar test while quietly poisoning the kidneys and destroying red blood cells. It's a masterclass in how biological deception can make a deadly disease look like a cure.
teenKit.whyItMatters: It proves that a single medical test score is useless—and sometimes fatal—if you don't understand the invisible biochemical machinery generating it.
keyTakeaways: Vanadate acts as a molecular imposter, structurally mimicking a phosphate group to jam itself into cellular machinery like PTP1B and trick the body into an insulin-like response.
Unregulated supplements can cause hidden catastrophic damage, such as kidney failure and hemolytic spherocytosis, even when lab numbers look completely normal.
A falsely normal Hemoglobin A1c can happen when red blood cells are prematurely destroyed, shortening their lifespan and hiding true, out-of-control blood sugar.
